summary:
No trans-specific incident series was found for Papua, but the dossier documents 138 recorded acts of torture or other ill-treatment in detention committed by police and military in Maybrat and the Central Highlands between September 2021 and Q1 2025, "with almost no consequences"; most victims were young men, several minors, arrested chiefly for alleged links to armed groups or protest participation. Named arbitrary-detention cases include three Papuans detained by officers at Nop Goliat Airport, Dekai (Yahukimo) on 26 July 2025 as two of them were preparing to depart for Jayapura to continue their studies. Q3 2025 saw a notable increase in military deployments and operations in the highlands, causing further internal displacement. For any visitor, including a transgender one, the probability that police contact escalates into unlawful detention and ill-treatment is documented and far above the national average. This is an amplifier finding on non-trans-specific evidence, not an independent conclusion about trans people.

It sits at the same level as West Sumatra (0.11) in deviation from the national score, though the mechanism differs: West Sumatra has an enacted bylaw with specified administrative penalties; Papua has a documented torture-and-arrest pattern that raises the severity of any encounter with security forces, without a trans-specific legal basis being needed.

sources.summary: TAPOL briefing (July 2025): police and military in West Papua committed 138 recorded acts of torture or ill-treatment in detention in Maybrat and the Central Highlands (Sept 2021-Q1 2025) with almost no consequences; victims mostly males under 24 plus 7 women and 7 minors; arrests largely for alleged armed-group links or demonstrations; deaths during torture documented in operation areas; incidents catalogued on the 'Papuans Behind Bars' database.

Human Rights Monitor case file: police arbitrarily detained three Papuans (Stevanus Silak, Eben Sobolim, Ami Sobolim) at Nop Goliat Airport, Dekai, Yahukimo on 26 July 2025 - two were preparing to fly to Jayapura to continue their studies, one an airport employee accompanying them; an example of airport-stop arbitrary detention any traveller can be swept into.

HRM Papua quarterly report Q3 2025 ('Justice Denied'): notable increase in military deployments and operations in West Papua's highland regions since August 2025, further internal displacement, fatal shootings and arbitrary detentions, and failure of accountability mechanisms.

tangentialFactors: The new national KUHP (Jan 2026) applies fully in Papua; the region-specific factor is not an anti-LGBT bylaw (none found) but a documented security-force abuse pattern that worsens any police contact, including for gender-nonconforming travellers.
